Keeps the pointer inside a window until [UnlockMouse](UnlockMouse) is called. This is what a first person camera or a map that scrolls at the screen edge needs: the pointer cannot leave and click on something else.

With the default of 0 the pointer is kept in the window that Graphics or Graphics3D created. With the handle of a window or gadget made by CreateWindow, CreateCanvas and friends, the pointer is kept inside the area of that window (the part inside its frame) or gadget instead. The area follows the window when it is moved or resized, and the lock ends by itself when the window or gadget is freed.

The lock does not change what [MouseX](MouseX), [MouseY](MouseY), [MouseXSpeed](MouseXSpeed) and [MouseYSpeed](MouseYSpeed) report, only where the pointer can go. It works together with [MoveMouse](MoveMouse), [HidePointer](HidePointer) and [RawInputs](RawInputs). Losing the focus does not end the lock: the pointer is free while another program is in front and is kept again when the window gets the focus back. Calling LockMouse again moves the lock to the new window. Without a graphics window the call is remembered and applies as soon as one is there.

```blitzbasic
Graphics 640, 480, 0, 2
SetBuffer BackBuffer()
LockMouse
HidePointer
While Not KeyHit(1)
	Cls
	Text 10, 10, "The pointer cannot leave the window. Escape ends"
	Text 10, 30, "Speed: " + MouseXSpeed() + ", " + MouseYSpeed()
	Flip
Wend
UnlockMouse
ShowPointer
```
@param window  Handle of the window or gadget to keep the pointer in. Optional, 0 is the window that Graphics created.
@gap This is a BlitzLLVM extension: the original has no such command.
